thread:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a 200–400ms P99 blip on a few long-context runs this morning, correlated with high KV churn under load :eyes:
Jon: Which shard / config? FIFO or LRU is enabled?
Maria: Dedicated host pool A, default governor (adaptive). Policy switched to FIFO under pressure. Repro attempt on staging shows same pattern.
Ravi: Interesting. I remember a race we had where FIFO reinserts + pager wakes caused thundering reserializations. Could be reinsert-path cost.
Sasha: Do we have a flame or perf profile from the spike window?
Maria: Uploaded a small perf dump to the task: link https://artifacts/internal/4998/kv-blip-4998001234-heap.svg — main hotspot is kv_reinsert_batch + page_scan_loop
Jon: Can you paste the hotspot snippet?
Maria: Sure:
```
# top stacks sampled during 4998001234 window
kv_reinsert_batch  42%
page_scan_loop     27%
lru_mark_touch     8%
fifo_reinsert_path 6%
other              17%
```
Ravi: kv_reinsert_batch at 42% screams batching heuristics failing — batcher draining too frequently and triggering many small reinsert ops.
Kevin: We recently tuned batch timeout down to 5ms for latency SLOs. Under heavy churn small batches could amplify reinserts.
Sasha: So kernel selection + batching interacts with eviction policy. If kernel picks slow memcpy path for large KV pages, reinserts cost multiplies.
Maria: Also observed that KV page fragmentation increased ~18% during spike window (see metric kv_fragmentation_pct). That increases the number of pages to scan.
Jon: Do we have a repro script to push into a loop? If yes we can toggle LRU vs FIFO and batch timeout to measure delta.
Maria: I pushed a repro to staging: `scripts/kv_stress_long_contexts.sh --pattern=reuse-skew --duration=5m`
Ravi: I'll run two experimental builds: (A) batch_timeout=20ms + LRU bias, (B) batch_timeout=5ms + FIFO (current). Will capture traces.
CiBot: Deploy scheduled: test/kvsim-4998001234-A -> vm-staging-7 at 4998001300 by Ravi
Kevin: Quick sanity: check KV eviction correctness — there was a subtle bug where FIFO reinserts didn't update last_touch, leading to premature eviction. Could cause reuse misses and more reinserts.
Sasha: If correctness bug exists we should prioritize a fix even if perf looks fine. Reuse miss loop will fluster any heuristic.
Maria: Agreed. I ran a quick unit check on reinserts and found an edge where reinserts could race with pager reclaim and lose a promoted bit. Adding an atomic set fixes it locally.
Jon: Nice. After Ravi's runs, can we collate: P99 latency, token throughput, kv_fragmentation_pct, reinserts/sec, page_scan_ops?
Ravi: Yep. Will post results in this thread. Running A now.
Maria: Thanks — if A reduces P99 by >25% we can consider fallback policy: prefer LRU under high churn or increase batch window.
Kevin: Also add a small kernel tweak: prefer memcpy path for page-sized moves on our NVMe host. That helped another cluster.
Sasha: Action items: 1) Ravi runs A/B and posts metrics (Ravi). 2) Maria prepares small atomic patch for reinserts (Maria). 3) Jon to spec fallback policy for governor (Jon). 4) Kevin to prototype memcpy preference (Kevin).
Jon: I'll start an RFC for governor fallback tonight.
CiBot: Test run complete: test/kvsim-4998001234-A -> vm-staging-7 ended at 4998001399 (results pending)
Ravi: Posting quick numbers: A (20ms+LRU) P99 220ms, reinserts/sec 3.1k, fragmentation 12% ; B (5ms+FIFO) P99 340ms, reinserts/sec 8.9k, fragmentation 18%
Maria: That's quite clear. LRU + larger batch window reduces churn & fragmentation.
Sasha: Great repro. Let's file a short perf regression ticket and schedule a canary rollout for the reinserts atomic fix + governor fallback.
Maria: Filing ticket now: https://issues/internal/INF-7321 — summary: "KV reinserts race + FIFO under low-batch-time causes P99 spikes", added logs and repro.
Kevin: If RFC for memcpy kernel change is small we can ship with canary too.
Jon: Cool. Moving to implement fallback and monitor. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
